_note: Indian-origin deities in Japan. Wording describes historical associations and syncretic origins ('developed from', 'associated with'), never identity. Every entry is needs-review until the owner verifies the site, wording and references. 'visiting' stays null until practical info is verified. 'label' is the map-label offset from the pin, in pixels on a 750px-wide map.

deities.story: Developed from the Indian river goddess Saraswati. Associated with music, eloquence and water, and often shown playing a biwa lute.
Developed from Ganesha (Vinayaka) through esoteric Buddhism. Often shown as a pair of embracing elephant-headed figures and associated with removing obstacles.
Developed from Lakshmi (Shri). Associated with good fortune, beauty and prosperity.
Developed from Mahakala, a fierce form associated with Shiva, and later blended with the Shinto god Ōkuninushi into a smiling god of the harvest and kitchens.
Developed from Vaishravana, guardian of the north, who is associated with Kubera. In Japan he became an armoured protector.
